summary: First end-to-end test of QueueFlow. Backend pytest suite (26 tests) covers auth, role guards, jobs CRUD, priority ordering (with max_workers=1), admin settings/audit/users, stats, health, live pending->running transition. All 26 backend tests PASSED. Frontend Playwright covered: register->/dashboard, job submit + kanban board + description clearing + modal, /admin guard for user, logout clears token, invalid login toast, admin login lands on /admin with audit panel, users table has >=2 rows, settings page slider+save button visible. All 10 frontend checks PASSED.

issues: Radix Dialog missing aria-describedby / DialogDescription (console warning, not a functional bug)

action_items: Optional: add <DialogDescription> (or aria-describedby='...') inside JobModal DialogContent to remove the a11y warning.
Optional: seed_admin's `if not verify_password(...)` on every startup does a bcrypt.checkpw; harmless but adds ~200ms to boot; consider caching.

CORS_ORIGINS='*' with allow_credentials=True is a known FastAPI/Starlette misconfig (browsers reject wildcard + credentials). Not blocking Bearer auth today since the app uses Authorization header, but tighten origins for production.
critical_code_review_comments: worker.py priority scheduling relies on client-side sort of a limited 20-doc find; if pending backlog >20 low-priority jobs older than a newly submitted high-priority job, the high job could starve behind the top-20 low jobs. Prefer server-side sort with a compound (priority DESC, created_at ASC) index (already exists) using find({status:'pending'}).sort([('priority',-1),('created_at',1)]).limit(1).

routes_jobs.retry_job/cancel_job/delete_job: audit is only logged when admin acts on another user's job; if the same admin acts on their own job it's not logged. Acceptable per spec ('admin action on someone else's job') but worth clarifying.
CORS wildcard + allow_credentials=True is invalid combo (Starlette will strip credentials); either enumerate origins or set allow_credentials=False.
routes_stats.get_stats reads all matching jobs into memory to compute counts; use Mongo aggregation for scale.
test_credentials: Admin laluchacha4@gmail.com / Admin@12345 (seeded). Test users created dynamically per test run with TEST_ prefix.
seed_data_creation: Each pytest run creates 1-2 TEST_user_<uuid>@example.com users plus assorted TEST-labelled jobs; no cleanup implemented since data uses TEST_ prefix and does not conflict with real data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_queueflow_api.py and is fully re-runnable via `pytest /app/backend/tests -v`. It resets max_workers to 2 at the end of the priority test. Priority test intentionally sets max_workers=1 briefly to serialize execution. If retesting after code changes to worker.py, note that priority test depends on the scheduler picking up new setting within ~1s (poll_interval).
